Full mode drags one visible mesh node to another to add a merge edge.

CERTIFY REPAIRED BRANCH submits the transcript; the full rendered interface has no keyboard handler for task controls.

autonomous_processes: None: the generated specimen, node coordinates, initial edges, focus, and camera are initialized once; the mechanic has no timer, animation loop, physics tick, or input-independent random update.

Only synchronous input handlers change focus, camera, seeds, edges, and the post-edit inspection gate; certification or a failed submission can trigger a rerender, but neither is autonomous idle evolution.
grouped_control_modes: D_merge: full mesh-node drag merge, which adds one missing edge.
D_split: full slice-node seed placement in the two colours followed by CUT BETWEEN SEEDS, which removes one false edge.
View-only modes: linked-plane scroll and empty-glass orbit change the visible focus or camera but do not change topology.
Administrative mode: CERTIFY REPAIRED BRANCH submits the final result and does not repair topology.

clause_i.reason: For the repair modes, an action-only policy cannot select the seed-dependent opaque node pair from I_t alone across generated instances; the missing and false edges vary with the seeded geometry and are not encoded in public labels.

clause_ii.reason: The needed geometry and current topology persist in the linked slices and reconstruction, so the current screenshot together with prior actions is sufficient in principle; no frame-to-frame observation is needed and a zero-length window would suffice for this clause.

clause_iii.reason: No autonomous non-clock task-state evolution occurs between actions: nodes, edges, focus, camera, seeds, and available repair controls remain unchanged while idle. The inspection gate is set synchronously by a merge or split action, and the 180-second allowance is only a deadline. Therefore no Delta > 0 makes an available repair action strictly less effective while success remains possible.

common_visible_process: None. The visible specimen is a static generated state; there is no common autonomous process whose evolution could both determine a delayed action and degrade its opportunity.

pre_run.reason: This configuration already fails the mathematical real-time definition because clause (iii) fails, so the pre-run threshold cannot change the label. No pre-run rate is estimated.

source_evidence.claim: The assigned difficulty-2 profile has three fibres, seven segments per fibre, one missing join, one false join, nine slices, and crossing density 0.47.

Full interaction is linked-plane scrolling, mesh orbit by dragging, mesh-node merge dragging, and slice-node seed placement; the task settings are 180 seconds, a zero-millisecond observation window, and one frame.

The launcher control condition selects the requested profile, and generation creates seeded static coordinates and initial/true edges, records the fixed focus and slice contract, and returns the public state without any future process.
Rendering initializes the model from the fixed state and exposes linked canvases, a mesh, full-mode seed/cut controls, and certification.

State changes are attached to synchronous click, wheel, pointer, and submit handlers: slice focus, orbit, edges, seeds, inspection gating, and rerendering change only in response to input or submission.
The mechanic CSS supplies layout and styling only and defines no animation or timed state transition.

The grader replays a finite event list from the initial topology, applies repair edits and inspection requirements synchronously, and validates the final graph; it has no task-time or autonomous evolution.
Verification only loads the exported result and invokes the Branch Repair grader.

The normal interaction sequence collects persistent slice views, orbits, repairs missing/false joins, inspects after edits, and certifies; the short waits are Playwright synchronization rather than task mechanics.
